threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: When you ask for a lemonade and get a confused look, only to find out they don’t serve anything that isn’t artisan or organic.
Last night on the 40, a couple were arguing over a bag of chips. The guy ended up throwing them out the window. Classic late-night drama.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I was waiting for the bus on Sonnenallee and overheard a guy argue passionately about the best Döner in town. That's when it hit me—this is home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg will you find a mural dedicated to a cat that lived in a specific yard for years—it's like a neighborhood mascot with its own street cred.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: True locals know that the sound of sirens means your brunch plans just went sideways. If they don't flinch, they're in it for the long haul.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full tuxedo get off a Muni bus, take a quick selfie with a pigeon, then hop on a scooter. Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just Gaudí and hipster bars. They miss the quiet corners where old ladies still gossip over daily groceries.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell when someone’s new; they’re the ones who still look lost trying to navigate the L1 line on a Sunday.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look baffled when the bus driver shouts ‘next stop’ and it’s not even a stop. Locals just nod and scroll.
Caught a night bus from Brixton last week, and a guy was singing opera on the top deck. Couldn’t tell if he was brilliant or just mad. The driver didn't even blink.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When the baker greets you by name and knows your favorite bread, that’s when you know this isn’t just a place you live, it’s home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Kreuzberg, you can find a spontaneous dance party at a bus stop. You'd think it's just the buses, but sometimes, the beats take over.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they can name at least three taco trucks that don’t have long lines after midnight.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Watched a guy in a full suit hop on the 38 at Civic Center, grabbed a seat, then pulled out a ukulele. Only in SF, right?

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all locals hang out at Park Güell, but the real vibe is at Plaça de la Vila, especially during the evening when the kids play and neighbors chat.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They’re the ones staring at the metro map like it's a treasure map, fumbling for the right line even after a month here.
